clue.text: Pest made ill by flight

indicators.note: being ill means in a bad way, so the letters of pest made are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A pest made poorly by a flight of stairs or a plane journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A panicked rush of a herd, as in fleeing in a mass, is a flight of animals.

clue.text: A heavenly creature's turn of phrase

indicators.note: a turn here means a twist or change of order, so the letters of phrase are turned about

explanation.surface: An angel has a pretty way with words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn of' rearranges PHRASE; the 's of the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the highest order of angels, the six-winged beings in Isaiah, is a heavenly being.

clue.text: Promise to take the chump on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a chump is a fool, an ass
the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Someone vows to bring a fool out on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places ASS above URE in the down light. The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a solemn guarantee to someone, pledging that something will happen, is to reassure them by vow.

clue.text: Cleared about a couple of pounds without colouring

indicators.note: about means round, so the paid word goes round the pound letters

parts.note: a debt cleared is one paid
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra), so two pounds give LL

explanation.surface: A settled bill of a couple of quid leaves something drab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleared' reads as tidied, but here it means a debt settled; 'about' is the containment signal, with L the standard abbreviation for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any hue, pale and wan, is a synonym sense.

clue.text: Makes little of many spring storms

parts.note: DI is 501 in Roman numerals, a large number standing for many
a spa is a mineral spring
storms, as a verb, means rages

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a whole season of spring gales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' gives DI as the Roman numerals for 501, a number used loosely for a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle or speak slightingly of something is a direct synonym.

clue.text: A fortifying drink or two-right?

parts.note: a brace is a pair, two of something such as game birds

explanation.surface: A stiff drink, or perhaps a couple, would be just right.
explanation.walkthrough: A brace is two, as in a brace of pheasants.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot of spirits taken to steady the nerves is a stiffener or pick-me-up.

clue.text: He'll express his views about a certain issue with some hesitation

parts.note: re means about or concerning
issue means offspring, and a particular one is a son
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone airs opinions on a particular question while hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means children, not a topic; the surface wants a debating point.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues logically and states conclusions is one who thinks things through.

clue.text: Place in the West Country continuing to defer payment

parts.note: to give credit is to let payment be put off
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: A town in the West Country keeps buying on tick.
explanation.walkthrough: Crediton is a small town in Devon, in England's West Country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Devon market town is an example of a location in south-west England.

clue.text: Presented an account for wine in a rush container

indicators.note: the reed is the container holding the wine inside it

parts.note: a rush is a marsh plant, a reed
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: An account of wine kept in a hollow reed vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' suggests hurry, but it is the marsh plant; 'container' signals that the plant word wraps the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Gave a description of events, told of them, is the past tense sense.

clue.text: Not settled, so not given support

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a cue or arm
less means without, not given something

explanation.surface: Someone unsettled because nobody backs them.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading the answer as REST-LESS gives 'without support'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to keep still or be calm is fidgety and uneasy.

clue.text: Come to terms with embellishment

definitions.meaning: to have reconciled after a quarrel

explanation.surface: Settling a dispute while adding flourishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarrellers who reconcile have patched it up; a story with invented details, or a face with cosmetics on, is fabricated or painted.

clue.text: Some article written about one's backer

indicators.note: the article is written next to the other pieces, following them

parts.note: part means some of something
one is I and 's is S
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Part of a newspaper piece is about a supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' gives I and S; 'written about' sets AN after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A committed supporter of a cause or party is a follower or champion.

clue.text: A supplier of basic knitwear

parts.note: basic knitwear read as the plain knitted garments worn on the legs and feet, sold by a tradesman

explanation.surface: A trader dealing in simple knitted clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in stockings and socks is a seller of legwear.

clue.text: Holds until immobile

parts.note: a shop holds stock, so holds means stocks
till means until

explanation.surface: Someone waits frozen until something happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely motionless, not stirring at all, is the idiom.

clue.text: The racket fought with foreign money

parts.note: battled means fought
the ore is a Scandinavian coin, a hundredth of a krone

explanation.surface: A noisy fight broke out over foreign cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests noise, but it is the bat used in an old shuttlecock game.
explanation.definitionFit: The bat used in the early form of badminton is a type of racquet.

clue.text: Prompt acknowledgments of indebtedness can appear phoney

parts.note: spur means prompt or urge
IOUs are notes acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: Quick IOUs can look fake.
explanation.definitionFit: False or not genuine is a synonym sense.

clue.text: Coppers involved receive notice

parts.note: P stands for pence, the copper coins

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of receive are mixed up

explanation.surface: Police officers taking part get a warning notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but it is P for pence. 'involved' rearranges RECEIVE into ERCEIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To become aware of something by seeing it is to spot or observe it.

clue.text: A wrecker of footwear on back street in Paris

indicators.note: in a down clue the clog sits on top, so it comes first

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog

indicators.note: back means the French street word is read backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A vandal of shoes on a back street in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RUE into EUR; 'on' puts SABOT above it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who deliberately damages machinery or plans is a destroyer.

clue.text: Pen a clever correction of commonness

indicators.note: a correction puts things in a new order, so the letters of pen a clever are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smart pen correcting something ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: How widespread something is, its frequency, is its being common.

clue.text: Showing a key on a ring

indicators.note: in a down clue the key sits on top, so it comes first

parts.note: B is a musical key
taken as written

explanation.surface: Displaying a key hung on a key ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing or uncovering something is revealing it.

clue.text: Going up a track

parts.note: a scent is the trail an animal leaves, which hounds track

explanation.surface: Following a trail uphill.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb or rise is the act of moving upwards.

clue.text: Partnered in duet rendition

indicators.note: a rendition is a performance or version, so the letters of in duet are rendered anew

explanation.surface: Paired off in a performance of a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined together or married is being linked as a pair.

clue.text: The minister causing a builder to lose his head

indicators.note: losing a head means the first letter goes from the builder word

parts.note: an erector is one who puts up structures

explanation.surface: A clergyman makes a construction worker lose his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England is a clergyman.

clue.text: Killer has two fools with popular following

indicators.note: the popular word follows the two fools
two means the fool word appears twice

parts.note: an ass is a fool
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A murderer with two idiots in tow is a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired murderer of a prominent person is a murderer.

clue.text: Twist maybe, and live surrounded by gold

indicators.note: the word live is put inside the gold word

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A twist of fate: living a life wrapped in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' looks like a turn, but it is Oliver Twist, the Dickens orphan; 'maybe' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is the Dickens orphan, so the hero's first name is an example of one named Twist.

clue.text: Conscientious trainee in editing possibly

indicators.note: in places the trainee letter inside the rearranged word
possibly signals the letters of editing may be arranged another way

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A careful trainee working in editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges EDITING; 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-working and careful in one's duties is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cattle drives

explanation.definitionFit: Castrated bulls raised for meat are bullocks; to guide a car is to direct its course.

clue.text: Rebuffed small-boned journalist

parts.note: slight means slender, of slim build
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A slim reporter was snubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Snubbed or insulted by being ignored is a synonym sense.
